title: Branches and Pull Requests for Teams: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on team Git workflow: feature branches, naming, staying current with main, opening and reviewing pull requests, GitHub merge options and branch protection.

chapters.title: Branches and PRs: The Mental Model
points: A branch is just a movable pointer to a commit; creating one copies no files, so branches are cheap and short-lived by design
A pull request is a GitHub request to merge a head branch into a base branch, with discussion, review and CI checks attached to it
Feature-branch flow: main stays deployable, all work happens on a branch off main, and the PR is the gate back into main
Branch naming convention: type/short-topic in lowercase kebab case, e.g. feat/login-form, fix/null-cart, chore/bump-deps
Keep branches short-lived and small: a PR under ~400 changed lines gets real review, a huge one gets a rubber stamp

chapters.title: Core Workflow: Branch to Merge
points: Loop: update main, branch off, commit, push, open PR, review, fix, merge, delete branch
Start clean: git switch main && git pull --ff-only && git switch -c feat/login-form
First push sets upstream: git push -u origin feat/login-form; after that plain git push works
Open the PR from the pushed branch (GitHub link in push output, or gh pr create --fill); mark Draft when work is not ready for review
Address review feedback with new commits on the same branch; the PR updates automatically on push
After merge, clean up: git switch main && git pull && git branch -d feat/login-form (remote branch deleted via GitHub button or auto-delete setting)

chapters.title: Keeping a Branch Up to Date
points: Fetch first: git fetch origin shows what changed upstream without touching your branch
Merge option: git merge origin/main adds a merge commit, keeps history exactly as it happened, safe on shared branches
Rebase option: git rebase origin/main replays your commits on top of main, giving linear history but rewriting commit hashes
Rule: rebase only commits nobody else has pulled; after rebasing a pushed branch use git push --force-with-lease, never plain --force
Conflict handling: edit the marked files, git add them, then git merge --continue or git rebase --continue; bail out with --abort
GitHub's Update branch button merges base into your branch; use it for quick catch-up, rebase locally if the team wants linear history

chapters.title: Opening and Reviewing a Pull Request
points: Good PR title and description: what changed, why, how it was tested, linked issue (Closes #123 auto-closes it on merge)
Self-review the diff on GitHub before requesting reviewers; remove debug code and unrelated changes
Reviewer outcomes: Comment (no verdict), Approve, Request changes (blocks merge when protection requires reviews)
Etiquette: review the code not the person, ask questions instead of commanding, prefix minor items with nit:, explain why for blockers
Author etiquette: respond to every comment, resolve threads only after fixing or agreeing, do not force-push mid-review without saying so
Respond quickly: aim to review within one working day; small PRs get reviewed faster

chapters.title: GitHub Merge Options and Branch Protection
points: Merge commit: keeps all branch commits plus a merge commit; full history, noisiest log
Squash and merge: collapses the PR into one commit on main; clean log, but loses per-commit detail and the branch's commits no longer match main
Rebase and merge: replays each commit onto main with new hashes, linear history with no merge commit
Branch protection rules on main: require pull request before merging, required approvals count, required status checks, require branches up to date, block force pushes and deletions
Require CODEOWNERS review so changes to owned paths need the owning team's approval; enable dismiss stale approvals on new pushes
Common mistake: admins bypassing protection, or squash merging a long-lived branch then reusing it, causing duplicate-commit conflicts on the next PR

chapters.title: Branches and PRs Cheat Sheet
points: Create and switch: git switch -c type/topic; list: git branch -vv; delete merged: git branch -d name
Sync: git fetch origin; git merge origin/main or git rebase origin/main; then git push --force-with-lease if rebased
Publish: git push -u origin branch; gh pr create --fill; gh pr checkout 123 to review locally
Merge choice: merge commit = full history, squash = one clean commit per PR, rebase = linear with all commits
Protection checklist: require PR, approvals, status checks, up-to-date branch, no force push, CODEOWNERS
Top mistakes: huge PRs, rebasing shared branches, plain --force, committing straight to main, reusing a squash-merged branch
